subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw narrow shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol` to `http/protobuf` now with this doctor migration, or keep accepting `grpc` until real gRPC exporter support exists?
rationale: The code path is coherent, but removing a shipped config value and choosing how doctor rewrites active telemetry configs is a compatibility policy choice that automation should not decide unilaterally.

options.title: Accept the narrow contract
options.body: Land the PR as the lower-risk fix: reject unsupported `grpc`, keep env overrides fail-closed, and let doctor remove legacy config while preserving the previous no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

options.title: Hold for real gRPC support
options.body: Pause or close this PR and instead implement gRPC exporters, dependency/package updates, endpoint/header semantics, docs, and live collector proof.

options.title: Request different migration semantics
options.body: Ask for a revised doctor policy if maintainers want old configs to remain accepted or want a different disable/preserve rule during upgrade.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow contract
recommendation.body: Land the PR as the lower-risk fix: reject unsupported `grpc`, keep env overrides fail-closed, and let doctor remove legacy config while preserving the previous no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to the original diagnostics exporter/config surface and the doctor migration framework, making them the best available routing owner for the compatibility decision.
